android.name: Android
android.used_by_emulator: Used by the emulator {{.Emulator}}. Delete the emulator first if you don't need it.
android.avds.title: Emulators
android.avds.what: Android Virtual Devices from Android Studio's Device Manager, with the apps and data installed on them.
android.avds.why: An emulator can be created again in Device Manager. Running emulators can't be selected.
android.avds.after: Apps and data inside the emulator are lost.
android.system_images.title: System images
android.system_images.what: Android versions that emulators boot from, about 2–4 GB each.
android.system_images.why: Images that no emulator uses can be downloaded again in Android Studio › SDK Manager. Images used by an emulator can't be selected.
android.system_images.after: To create an emulator with this Android version you'll need to download the image again.
android.ndk.title: NDK versions
android.ndk.what: Native Development Kit versions used to compile C/C++ code in Android and React Native projects.
android.ndk.why: Gradle downloads the NDK version a project asks for (ndkVersion) automatically when it's missing.
android.ndk.after: The next build of a project that needs this version will download it first.
android.sources.title: SDK sources
android.sources.what: The Java and Kotlin source code of Android itself, so the editor can show it when you open a class like Activity.
android.sources.why: Builds don't use it. Android Studio offers to download it again when you open a class without sources.
android.sources.after: Opening an Android class shows decompiled code until you download the sources again.
